message.content: In lions, one of the most noticeable dominant traits is the **presence of a mane in adult male lions**. While the mane’s exact size and darkness are influenced by hormones (particularly testosterone) and environmental factors, the underlying genetic predisposition for a mane is dominant. This means that if a lion inherits the allele for a mane from either parent, it will typically develop one.
